parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as a clean-room reimplementation of StGit, using bundled docs and executable interaction while avoiding source lookup or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated documentation/help probing and CLI behavior probing to children while continuing its own probing and implementation, leaving the live shared executable as a shared reference and deliverable.
parallel.implementation: A child created /workspace/stg.py and a compile script that copied it into /workspace/executable; the parent later rebuilt a Python implementation under src/stg.py with captured help text.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration recovered by overwriting the child-mutated executable from the parent's src implementation and cleaning stray child artifacts before packaging the final tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran many smoke probes and final command checks, but those checks had to account for a contaminated help capture after the original binary had been replaced.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final answer admits several explicit stubs, including uncommit, and the official evaluator failed the solution despite 1228 passing tests.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room StGit replacement task and used only allowed interaction with the bundled executable and local documentation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent owned probing, implementation, preservation of the original reference binary, executable replacement, and verification without delegated child ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: It added a large Git-backed src/stg.py implementation, then created compile.sh and a bash executable wrapper that invoked that source implementation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It first moved the original executable to reference-executable, then added the replacement executable and chmodded the final entrypoints, avoiding mid-probe reference loss.
serial.verification: It ran py_compile and multiple side-by-side scenario diffs against reference-executable, including commit/uncommit, stack operations, content inspection, branch operations, and help/version smoke tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final answer still acknowledged that less-exercised StGit subcommands outside the tested set were not implemented, and the official evaluator failed the solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the clean-room executable-replacement requirement and the prohibition on source lookup or wrapping.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received and followed the same clean-room reverse-engineering prompt and constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; the later difference was workspace handling of the reference executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent spawned docs_probe and cli_probe children while it also continued local probing and implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had multi-agent disabled and no child threads, so one agent owned the entire lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced concurrent ownership of the workspace and executable reference; serial did not have a child ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and children did not maintain a protected boundary between the reference binary, the submitted executable, and implementation artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent made the boundary explicit by moving the original binary to reference-executable before adding the replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial path preserved an oracle for comparisons, while the parallel path allowed a child to mutate the oracle before parent probing was finished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ended with a Python implementation under src/stg.py plus compile.sh and captured help text, but its path included recovery from child mutation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a Python src/stg.py, then installed a bash executable wrapper that invoked it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used Python reimplementation strategies, but serial implemented uncommit in the exercised set while parallel final listed uncommit among explicit stubs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After detecting the executable mutation, the parent listed active children and interrupted cli_probe and docs_probe rather than waiting for normal returned results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join or inspect, because the execution protocol disabled multi-agent use.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child lifecycle disruption as a downstream correction to the overwrite; serial avoided that lifecycle entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The docs_probe child wrote compile.sh that copied /workspace/stg.py into /workspace/executable, and the parent later observed the executable had changed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent explicitly moved the original executable to reference-executable before adding the replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered a shared deliverable overwrite; serial sequenced reference preservation before replacement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run smoke-tested many commands but had to correct a mutated-binary help capture, then officially failed 1041 tests with 1228 passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run performed side-by-side comparisons against a preserved reference and final smoke tests, then officially failed 1053 tests plus one error with 1156 passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification used an intact reference binary; parallel verification was partially contaminated and repaired, though both remained incomplete under official testing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without host timeout after 1717 agent seconds, but closed with explicit stubs and cleanup of concurrent probe artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without host timeout after 1607 agent seconds and closed with residual unimplemented less-exercised subcommands.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra closure effort recovering from shared-state contamination; serial had a simpler closure path, though both stopped short of full behavioral coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is both_fail, not a discordant outcome. Parallel passed 1228 of 2289 tests and serial passed 1156 of 2289 tests, so the score gap alone does not establish a causal outcome difference. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel had to recover from a child overwriting the shared executable/oracle, while serial preserved the reference before replacement.
parallel_contributors: A child replaced the shared executable during ongoing parent probing, forcing recovery and correction of contaminated observations.
The final parallel implementation still listed many unimplemented subcommands, including uncommit.
serial_contributors: The serial agent preserved the original executable as reference-executable before installing the replacement.
The serial implementation covered uncommit in its exercised set but still failed hidden tests overall.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel final explicitly left uncommit as a stub, while serial claimed it implemented and tested commit/uncommit.
Both solutions were incomplete clean-room StGit reimplementations with many hidden-test failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event, not a pass/fail differential explanation
